svg.text: The service bay and a Casakin-class battlecruiser, at true scale · bow to the left · after the Master Specification, Rev 157
a Casakin rides in the service bay along the keel of midships
service bay 2,100 × 400 × 300 m · keel doors underneath
docking arms on the ventral flanks
Keep and command island, just forward of the bay
the bay's keel doors amidships, the Salvage Bay aft, four docking arms on the flanks
bay 400 m wide · 85 m clear of the hangar halls · 20 m below the Frigate Deck
Ballista turrets: four on the centerline, two on each shoulder
deck house over the jump-drive core
A 2,100 × 400 × 300 m vacuum bay along the keel of midships takes one
2 km battlecruiser with about twenty meters' clearance all round. The four
take it in turn for refit, and a Casakin whose jump drive has failed
rides in it through every jump until it is fixed.
With no Casakin in, all four Kangeths at once, or every frigate in the fleet.
How the hull is built around it.
The Keep sits just forward of the bay. Load paths run either side of it and
frames close around its keel doors, which fold back along the whole length
when a Casakin comes up from below.
Corricks berth on the Frigate Deck and Kangeths in the cargo bays; the
Casakins live alongside on four docking arms.
